answer.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Two archived memories (86 and 31) show that onboarding simplification and signup field reduction both drove durable activation lifts in self-serve cohorts without retention risk. Verifying these two records will confirm the magnitude and durability of those effects before committing to a standard experiment. Promotional pricing is rejected because memory_73 shows deep discounting harms renewal retention, creating unsustainable revenue. Referral incentives work well for established customers (memory_57) but won't address the immediate activation shortfall or competitive pressure on SMB. Activation messaging (memory_91) is plausible but onboarding has a clearer causal link to the observed 4% completion decline. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) addresses conversion for enterprise, not the current SMB activation crisis. Simplifying onboarding targets the measured drop directly, aligns with proven playbook, and avoids the revenue quality risk of discounting.
